s1.syndrome_frame: Acute scrotal swelling in a neonate with signs of infection
salient_findings: Pus-like discharge from an ulcerated area of the left hemi-scrotum
key_facts: Returned at four weeks of age
24-hour history of left scrotal swelling, erythema, fever, and pus-like discharge
Scrotal examination revealed a left scrotal abscess
Started on intravenous amoxicillin-clavulanate and flucloxacillin and fluids

raw.syndrome_frame: Acute scrotal swelling in a neonate with signs of infection
salient_findings: Pus-like discharge from an ulcerated area of the left hemi-scrotum
key_facts: Returned at four weeks of age
24-hour history of left scrotal swelling, erythema, fever, and pus-like discharge
Scrotal examination revealed a left scrotal abscess
Started on intravenous amoxicillin-clavulanate and flucloxacillin and fluids

shortlist.label: Neonatal testicular torsion
shortlist.why_kept: Acute scrotal swelling and hard, swollen testis

shortlist.label: Scrotal abscess
shortlist.why_kept: Pus-like discharge and scrotal examination findings

shortlist.label: Epididymitis
shortlist.why_kept: Signs of infection and scrotal swelling

shortlist.label: Fournier gangrene
shortlist.why_kept: Severe infection with ulceration and potential for rapid progression

raw.rationale: The presence of a pus-like discharge from an ulcerated area of the left hemi-scrotum and the scrotal examination revealing a left scrotal abscess support this diagnosis

rejected.label: Neonatal testicular torsion
rejected.why: Although considered, the presence of a scrotal abscess and infection signs point more towards an infectious process

rejected.label: Epididymitis
rejected.why: Epididymitis typically presents with pain and swelling of the epididymis, but the key finding here is the scrotal abscess

rejected.label: Orchitis
rejected.why: Orchitis is inflammation of the testis, which could be a component, but the primary issue appears to be the scrotal abscess

rejected.label: Fournier gangrene
rejected.why: Fournier gangrene is a severe, necrotizing infection of the genitalia, which is not indicated by the information provided
